You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: To what extent has the image been transformed from the source into a pencil drawing?
node.criteria: Pass only when the scene as a whole convincingly reads as a pencil drawing, with visibly pencil-like strokes, outlines, or drawn shading replacing the photographic rendering. Fail only when there is no observable drawing-like change toward that style compared with the source. Partial when credible drawing-like changes visibly alter the rendering but the transformation remains incomplete or weak and substantial photographic appearance remains. Softened or sketch-like contours and tonal texture may support progress only when they visibly change the rendering; desaturation, muted color, or grain alone is not progress. Unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to judge.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images for the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Apply the criteria explicitly: distinguish observable drawing-like progress from completion. Credible drawing-like changes with substantial photographic structure remaining are partial, not pass; pass requires a convincing pencil-drawn rendering across the scene as a whole. Do not count desaturation, muted color, or grain alone as progress or completion. Reserve fail for no observable requested progress; use unknown only when evidence is insufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a visibly drawn rendering across the scene: colors are largely reduced to muted pencil-like tones, and the food, glassware, and table setting show softened outlines and textured tonal shading rather than the source's crisp photographic appearance. The pencil-like treatment is apparent throughout, not just as desaturation or grain.

response.content: {"text":"The node already distinguishes progress from completion, but its trace shows it is collapsing “pencil-like” cues into a scene-wide pass: the edited image is strongly muted and grainy, while much of the food, glassware, and table still retains photographic shading and texture. Apply the existing completion threshold more strictly: require convincing drawn strokes/outlines or pencil-style shading across the scene, not merely softened contours and tonal texture; when genuine drawing-like changes are present but substantial photographic rendering remains, return partial. Ground the decision in specific regions and separate those cues from desaturation or grain. The trace is valid and has no dependency or transport failure, so this is a criterion-application/calibration issue, not missing evidence. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence."}
